newsitem.title: JAPAN: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Oct 31.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Oct 31.

text.p: Mitsui Fudosan Co Ltd is expected to post current losses of more than 40 billion yen in the business year to March 31, 1997. However, its net balance is expected to be in the black for the period. It will generate 50 billion yen in extraordinary income by selling about five billion shares in its affiliate, Oriental Land Co Ltd, an operator of Tokyo Disneyland, which is slated to be listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange in December.
Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp said it plans to offer a multimedia network service featuring a transmission speed of 10 megabits per second by 2005.

Cosmo Oil Co Ltd is expected to post parent current profits of less than four billion yen and General Sekiyu KK at slightly above four billion yen for the first half to September 30, down by half from the same period a year earlier. The reasons for the sharp drop are due to oil price rises and the yen's weakness.

Nippon Broadcasting System Inc, a company in the Fuji Sankei group, plans to apply to the Finance Ministry for permission to list its shares on the second section of the Tokyo Stock Exchange on December 2. It posted a current profit of 2.1 billion yen in the business year ended March 31, 1996, down 13 percent from a year earlier.

Chrysler Japan Sales Ltd, a Japanese unit of Chrysler Corp, plans to launch on November 8 a right-hand drive Jeep Wrangler to join the left-hand drive model already in the market. It plans to lower the price of the new model in spite of the strong dollar in an attempt to reverse slowing sales for Chrysler vehicles in Japan. It hopes for annual sales of 2,500 in 1997.

Teijin Ltd and Unitika Ltd have agreed to jointly develop polyester markets. The companies plan to set up a joint venture in April next year in Thailand, and later they may launch other joint ventures in Europe and China. They will be the first Japanese synthetic fibre producers to develop such products in overseas markets.
